paper_metadata.title: Thermal shock cycling behavior of NiCoCrAlYSiB coatings on Ni-base superalloys II. Microstructure evolution

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: NiCoCrAlYSiB coatings were obtained using an arc ion plating technique on a directionally solidified Ni-base superalloy.

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: Thermal shock resistance of the bare and coated superalloys were investigated by cycling between high temperature (900, 1000 and 1050 °C) and room temperature (forced water quenching).

evidence.section: 1. Introduction
evidence.quote: The high temperature strength of nickel-based superalloys is derived from the intermetallic Ni3(Al, Ti) precipitate distribution. These ordered precipitates, called γ′ precipitates, have an L12-type structure

evidence.section: 1. Introduction
evidence.quote: embedded in a nickel-rich disordered solid solution matrix called the γ phase

attributes.size: 2-3 μm in zone A, smaller in zone B

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure evolution in coated superalloys during thermal shock cycling
evidence.quote: The main coating (MC) is composed of γ + γ′ microstructure. The white colored particles have been identified as γ′ precipitates and the matrix is γ phase. The particle size and distribution of γ′ in this layer is not uniform. In zone marked “A”, we can see large γ′ particles with the size of 2–3 μm

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure evolution in coated superalloys during thermal shock cycling
evidence.quote: The size of the γ′ particles are only tens of nanometers. These γ′ particles are often called secondary γ′ precipitates [15].

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: A directional coarsening of the γ′ precipitates (γ′ rafting) just beneath the γ′-impoverishing zone (or interdiffusion zone) is observed.

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: phase transformation from γ′ to γ occurred at the surface of the coated and bare specimens due to the consumption of Al and Ti by oxidation.

evidence.section: 4.1. Microstructure evolution and influence of γ′ impoverishing on the crack formation and propagation
evidence.quote: Repeated formation and spallation of oxide scales in the coating surface consumed the Al content in the NiCoCrAlYSiB coatings. For the bare superalloys, not only Al, but also Ti was easy to be impoverished in the surface due to the easiness of the reaction of these elements with O. As a result, the γ′ phase transform into γ phase at the specimen surface.

mechanisms.name: crack formation by oxide breakdown and cyclic creep

evidence.section: 4.1. Microstructure evolution and influence of γ′ impoverishing on the crack formation and propagation
evidence.quote: But one contradicted factor discounts this and confirms that surface oxide breakdown and irreversible cyclic creep during thermal shock cycling accounts for the crack formation and propagation (Part I).

evidence.section: 4.1. Microstructure evolution and influence of γ′ impoverishing on the crack formation and propagation
evidence.quote: Cracks appeared to occur early in the coating life, with subsequent Al depletion in the cracked zones due to fast inward diffusion of O through the microcracks and crevices.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure evolution in coated superalloys during thermal shock cycling
evidence.quote: The very wide IZ region can be divided into two layers. The outer layer close to the coating is a γ zone, while microstructure of the inner layer adjacent to the substrate can be described as large amounts of very small γ′ precipitates besprinkled in the γ matrix.
